author: Linnaeus, 1758

art.subject: Bufflehead (Bucephala albeola), adult male in winter plumage, as worn from November to April: head black with a green and purple gloss, crossed by a large white patch that runs from just behind the eye over the back of the head; neck, breast, flanks and underparts white; back black; tail grey. Bill short, blue-grey; iris dark; legs and feet pink.
art.pose: swimming buoyantly in a sheltered bay between dives, side view
art.scene: sheltered Korean bay or estuary in winter, calm grey-blue water; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Very small diving duck, about the size of a Eurasian Teal and much smaller than Common Goldeneye; compact and round-bodied, floating high and buoyant. Head large and rounded for the body, puffy at the back, on a short neck. Bill short and stubby, much shorter than the head. Legs short, set far back. In flight the male shows a large white patch over the inner upperwing, the female a small white patch on the secondaries. Tail short, often resting on the water.
avoid: Do not paint the round white spot at the bill base of Common Goldeneye (Bucephala clangula); the Bufflehead's white is a large patch behind the eye.
Do not make it goldeneye-sized; it is tiny, about the size of a teal.
Do not paint a yellow iris; the eye is dark.
Do not give it the black eye mask, white crest or narrow saw-bill of Smew (Mergellus albellus).
